request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Explicit task constraints were lost during implementation.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Before making changes, restate and preserve every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint from the request."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A standing one-line instruction is cheaper than a procedural skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":3,"justification":"It tells the model to restate constraints before starting, but gives no mechanism to keep them enforced through the rest of the implementation, so the same mid-task drift could still recur."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":2,"justification":"\"Restate and preserve every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint\" is broad enough to cover the failure class but reads as a generic platitude without any concrete verification step (e.g., checklist or end-of-task re-check against the original request)."},"trigger_quality":{"score":3,"justification":"As a claude-md entry rather than a skill it doesn't need a \"Use when\" trigger, but its own condition (\"before making changes\") fires on virtually every task, so it offers little discrimination about when it actually matters."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text is fully generic with no project-, file-, or evidence-specific nouns leaked from the incident."},"routing_fitness":{"score":4,"justification":"A one-line standing global instruction is a cheap, proportionate fix for a generic constraint-tracking lapse, correctly avoiding heavier remedies like a skill or subagent for this kind of failure."}}

actionability.justification: It tells the model to restate constraints before starting, but gives no mechanism to keep them enforced through the rest of the implementation, so the same mid-task drift could still recur.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: "Restate and preserve every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint" is broad enough to cover the failure class but reads as a generic platitude without any concrete verification step (e.g., checklist or end-of-task re-check against the original request).

leakage.justification: The remedy text is fully generic with no project-, file-, or evidence-specific nouns leaked from the incident.

routing_fitness.justification: A one-line standing global instruction is a cheap, proportionate fix for a generic constraint-tracking lapse, correctly avoiding heavier remedies like a skill or subagent for this kind of failure.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md entry rather than a skill it doesn't need a "Use when" trigger, but its own condition ("before making changes") fires on virtually every task, so it offers little discrimination about when it actually matters.
